TA Code Spec

	This is the spec used for the basis of the Ruyle Lab code used for Processing of  Targeted Analysis Data. This document will outline in great detail and in written word, exactly what is done to the raw data in order to produce the final output dataset.

General Idea: Scientist will provide input data files. Code will output MDLs/MRLs, calculated amount values for each sample, Spike recovery, EIS Recovery, as well as a list of QC Flags. Scientist will interpret list of QC Flags and make any necessary adjustments to raw preprocessed data set. Scientist will run second section that reprocesses the adjusted dataset and delivers MDLs/MRLs, calculated amount values, spike recovery, EIS recovery, and list of QC Flags. Code ran on adjusted data set will be identical, just simply in another section of the notebook to keep it distinguished and the adjustments and reprocessing is visually present. 

Skeleton:  
Start →

1. Readfile  
2. RT Validation  
3. LOQ/ULOQ  
4. Censor based on LOQ/ULOQ  
5. Calculate and apply EF  
6. MDL/MRL  
7. Censor below MDL/MRL  
8. Spike Recovery  
9. EIS Recovery  
10. NIS Sensitivity  
11. Instrument Blank  
12. Check Standards

Output →

1. Calculated values of each compound per sample  
2. QC Summary  
3. QC Figures  
4. Copied Raw Data Set for making any QC adjustments

\[Scientist makes QC Adjustments to raw data here\]

Rerun →

1. Input QC adjusted dataset  
2. Same code processing as before

Output 2 →

1. Calculated values of each compound per sample  
2. QC Summary  
3. QC Figures

Section Details

1. Readfile  
   1. Code Prompts user to input folder location containing files with the following naming convention: 2026\_02\_05\_PFAS\_Quantitation\_ByCompound\_NS\_PFOA\_20260805172522  
   2. Code reads in all rows from all files and makes master list of entire dataset.   
   3. The following columns should have data recorded, any other column information is ignored.  
      1. Sample Raw File Name  
      2. Sample Type  
      3. Sample Name (Batch Ordering)  
      4. Sample ID  
      5. Compound Name  
      6. Detected Mass  
      7. Theoretical Amount  
      8. Method Apex RT  
      9. Calculated Amount  
      10. Peak Area  
      11. ISTD Compound Name  
      12. ISTD Amount  
      13. ISTD Area  
      14. ISTD Actual RT  
2. RT Validation  
   1. Every datapoint (target analytes and standards) must align within \+/- 0.4 min of RT observed in cal standard points. If a datapoint does not meet criteria, value is removed from dataset and future calculations.   
      1. Make list of all compounds based on unique values from Compound Name columns in master data set. This list will store values calculated per compound throughout this code and will be referred to as compound list.  
      2. For each compound, calculate the average RT value (from Method Apex RT column) of all rows with that compound in Compound Name Column and “Cal Std” in Sample Type Column. Add as component column to compound list.  
      3. Check all rows not labeled Cat Std in Sample Type column. The value in the  method apex RT column in these rows should be within \+/- 0.4 of the value generated in the previous calculation that has a matching Compound Name value.   
      4. If value does not fall within the \+/- 0.4 window, row is deleted from master list.  
3. LOQ/ULOQ Determination and Censorship  
   1. The LOQ & ULOQ will be determined for each compound by assessing the smallest and largest cal standard theoretical values present in the dataset. All data less than or greater than the LOQ & ULOQ respectively, will be removed from the master list.   
      1. For each compound in the compound list, determine the lowest value in the theoretical amount column in rows with sample type \= “Cal Std”. Set this value as the LOQ for this compound and add to compound list.  
      2. Similar to the first step, determine the highest value in rows with sample type=”Cal Std” per compound and set this value as ULOQ in the compound list.   
      3. For every row in the master list, if the value in calculated amount is less than the corresponding LOQ value for the compound matching in its compound name column, remove the value and replace with “\<LOQ”  
      4. For every row in the master list, if the value in calculated amount is greater than the corresponding ULOQ value for the compound matching in its compound name column, remove the value and replace with “\>ULOQ”  
4. EF Calculation and Application  
   1. The extraction factor for each sample is calculated and applied to all data corresponding to that sample. Extraction factor is calculated by taking the dilution factor of the final preparation step in our SOP (300 µL/135 µL) multiplied by the assumed blowdown sample volume (0.5 mL) divided by the actual sample mass (in grams). The actual sample mass in grams for each sample is prompted by the code and inputted by the Scientist.   
      1. For every unique value in “Sample Raw File Name” for rows with Sample Type \= “Unknown”, it is inputted into a list called sample list. This list will hold values specific to the sample similar to that created to hold values specific to each compound.   
      2. For every sample from the sample list, the code will prompt the scientist to input sample mass or volume. Append these inputted values under a sample mass or volume column in the sample list.   
      3. Calculate an Extraction Factor, labeled EF, for each sample. EF is calculated by: EF \= (300/135)\*(0.5/sample mass or volume)  
      4. Multiply calculated amount values in all rows in the master list with sample type=”Unknown” by the EF Corresponding to its value in Sample Raw File Name. If the calculated amount value is N/F, \<LOQ or \>ULOQ, leave the label as is and do not apply the EF.   
5. MDL/MRL Calculation and Censorship   
   1. Calculate an MDL and, when insufficient data is available, an MRL, for all compounds. The scientist is prompted to select the samples corresponding to the method blanks for their procedure. If a compound is detected in at least 3 of the method blanks, an MDL is calculated with the following formula: MDL \= Average of all values in identified method blanks \+ (t(n-1,0.99) \* Standard deviation of all values in identified method blanks). If there is an insufficient number of method blanks in which the compound is detected (n\<3), an MRL is calculated by multiplying the LOQ of that analyte by the average EF across all samples and method blanks.   
      1. Code prompts scientist to select samples from list of all sample names from sample list identifying the samples that operate as the method blank in their batch. Scientist selects samples.  
      2. For every compound (in compound list), if there are at least 3 identified method blanks that have a calculated amount value that is not N/F, \<LOQ, or \>ULOQ, an MDL is calculated. MDL \= Average of calculated amount values in rows corresponding to that compound and the identified method blank sample raw file name plus the t statistic corresponding to a df value equal to the number of method blanks minus 1 and a single-tailed 99th percentile multiplied by the standard deviation. Append MDL Value to compound list.  
      3. For every compound with less than 3 identified method blanks that contain a non-censored value, an MRL is calculated. MRL is calculated by multiplying the LOQ for that compound (from compound list) by the average EF across all values from sample list. Append MRL value to compound list.  
      4. Print MDL/MRLs for all compounds in a table.  
      5. All rows with value in the calculated amount column less than MDL or MRL (whichever is present) calculated for the compound corresponding to its value in the compound name column, is removed from the master list.     
6. Spike Recovery  
   1. A low and high spike recovery is calculated for every compound. The scientist inputs their low and high spike amounts (in ng), selects their low and high spike samples from the sample list, and inputs the sample mass for each. A nominal spike concentration is calculated by dividing the spike amount by the sample mass and multiplying by a spike factor. Samples are then selected as background, and the mean values of each analyte in the background samples are calculated. To calculate the spike recovery, the background mean values are subtracted from the values in the spiked samples and then divided by the nominal concentration multiplied by 100%.   
      1. Spike Factor values per compound are saved in the compound list.  
      2. Code requests input for low and high spike amounts from scientist (in ng) and records the value.   
      3. Code shows list of all samples and scientist selects the sample raw file name that corresponds to the low spikes. Code records selected sample    
      4.  Code shows list of all samples and scientist selects the sample raw file name that corresponds to the high spikes. Code records selected sample.  
      5. Code asks input of sample mass or volume for each of the selected low and high spike samples.   
      6.  Column for nominal concentrations created for compound list. Nominal concentrations of each compound in each of the low and high spiked samples is calculated by dividing the input spike amounts by the inputted sample mass or volume and multiplying the quotient by the Spike factor corresponding to that compound.   
      7. Code prompts scientist to select background samples from sample list.   
      8. Code prompts scientist to assign selected background samples to selected spiked samples (background samples will be used more than once)  
      9. Spike recovery for each compound in each identified spike sample is calculated by subtracting the mean of the calculated amount value in the background samples from the value in the spiked sample, then dividing by the nominal concentration value and multiplying by 100%. Save spike recovery for specific spike sample in compound list.  
7. EIS Recovery   
   1. EIS Recovery will be calculated in 2 different ways for every EIS compound in all of the samples of a given matrix. For example, in my method blank matrix (e.g., chicken), EIS recoveries for a compound will be calculated based on the average EIS recovery in each of the triplicate samples as well as the spiked samples. This will be repeated for all the samples in my target sample matrix (e.g., oyster). This section starts by prompting the scientist to create list names for matrix types and then select corresponding samples from sample list to add under each matrix.   
   2. An EIS Compound is built from all unique values from the ISTD Compound Name column in the master list. NIS Compound list is hard coded.   
   3. List of NIS to EIS assignments for the Method  2 calculation is hard coded and if there are EIS Compounds without an assigned NIS, scientist is prompted to input for each. Options include all NIS compounds from hard coded NIS list as well as an option to not input anything as there may not be a corresponding NIS for every EIS compound.  
   4. Method 1 \= EIS peak area in sample / mean EIS peak area across cal standards and instrument blanks. EIS peak area in all samples is retrieved from the ISTD Area column. Cal standard and instrument blank data is denoted by “Cal Std” and “Blank” in Sample Type Column from master list. The results for each compound in each sample should be appended to the EIS compound list.   
   5. Method 2 \= EIS calculated relative to NIS. Concentration of EIS compound calculated using ![][image1]then dividing by theoretical value of 5000 ng/L \*100% for EIS Recovery value. RF calculated for each EIS compound relative to its associated NIS in each cal standard using this formula:   
      (Area of EIS x Mass of NIS)/(Area of NIS x Mass of EIS)  
      Area of EIS \= value in ISTD Area  
      Mass of NIS \= value in Detected Mass for that particular sample in which compound name \= Compound from NIS list  
      Area of NIS \= value in Peak Area for that particular sample in which compound name \= Compound from NIS list.  
      Mass of EIS \= Value in detected mass for that particular sample in which compound name \= Compound from EIS list.  
      DF \= 1 (default). Scientist is prompted if a Dilution Factor other than 1 should be applied, then DF \= input value.  
      Ws \= sample mass or volume for that sample inputted in the EF section.  
      Append Method 2 calculated value to EIS list. There is a value for every EIS compound and every sample in a matrix from the prompt at the beginning of this section.  
   6. EIS Recovery values are flagged if recovery is outside of 70-130% Window.  
8. NIS Sensitivity   
   1. NIS Sensitivity is calculated for every NIS compound in every sample.   
   2. Divide NIS Peak area by mean NIS Peak area in cal standard points. Calculated for every NIS Compound in each sample. NIS Peak area \= value in Peak Area for that particular sample when Compound Name \= NIS Compound being assessed. The mean NIS Peak area in cal standard points is the average value in Peak Area of every sample with Sample Type \= Cal Std for that NIS Compound.  
   3. Flagged data if criteria outside of 50-150% is not met.   
9. Instrument Blank  
   1. Because MDL/MRL censoring has already been applied, any values of compounds not from EIS or NIS compound list that are observed in instrument blank samples should be flagged for QC concern. Instrument blank samples are denoted by Sample Type \= “Blank” from master list.  
10. Check Standard  
    1. The calculated amount value for each compound (not in NIS and EIS compound list) in samples denoted by Sample Type \= Check Standard should be within 70-130% of the value in Calculated Amount in the cal standard point with matching theoretical values.   
11. Final Output  
    1. Censored Data  
    2. QC Report   
    3. Figures
